### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via recordIds (symbol, a field of interface ExplainAccessRequest), recordIds (literal, a string literal in recordIds))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6af3d295757186a6e5299b4004d1810a9d144765` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3d62871e06a879c774bb36baa255a70d7180067c` — the merge of head `57913a379525abcbfb63ab4fba331fda9b2ce136` into base `6af3d295757186a6e5299b4004d1810a9d144765`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3d62871e06a879c774bb36baa255a70d7180067c && git checkout 3d62871e06a879c774bb36baa255a70d7180067c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6af3d295757186a6e5299b4004d1810a9d144765 57913a379525abcbfb63ab4fba331fda9b2ce136 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6af3d295757186a6e5299b4004d1810a9d144765 && git merge --no-ff 57913a379525abcbfb63ab4fba331fda9b2ce136

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6af3d295757186a6e5299b4004d1810a9d144765
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6af3d295757186a6e5299b4004d1810a9d144765` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `29000bb116f9b5f488199006631493dc75798cbe`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts + packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts, packages/rest/src/security-routes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-explain-access.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-security-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts, packages/spec/src/data/masked-field-types.ts (precedent), packages/spec/scripts/build-api-surface.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json, tsconfig.base.json. The changeset and `security-service.test.ts` are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs read: card #29297 (body, comments 6576596125, 6580454301, 6581669782), PR #29470 body and file list, `git diff origin/main...29000bb1` (3 files, +86/-2), the head's check-runs at 2026-11-02T16:02Z.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Caller-side accept set widens, nothing narrows — right.** `ISecurityService.explain(request)` (L1130) now accepts an object literal carrying `recordIds` without an excess-property error; every request that compiled on `main` (`object`, `operation`, `userId?`, `recordId?`) still compiles. The member is optional (`recordIds?: ExplainRequest['recordIds']`, L182).
2. **Implementer side stays assignable — right.** The only `ISecurityService` implementer in the tree is `security-plugin-security-service.ts` L344, which spreads the request into `SecurityPlugin.explainAccessForCaller`; the extracted body (`security-plugin-explain-access.ts` L128) already types the member `readonly string[]`, which accepts the contract's `string[]`. The structural slice in `plugin-sharing/sharing-service.ts` L479 takes `ExplainAccessRequest` itself; the `vi.fn` doubles in plugin-audit and service-storage take the contract type; the plugin-webhooks testkit stub declares a narrower parameter, which method bivariance still admits. No consumer is moved off the contract.
3. **Public surface: no export added, removed or renamed — right.** `build-api-surface.ts` records one `name (kind)` row per declared kind (header L13–16; members are ungated, L40), so the `ExplainAccessRequest (interface)` row in `api-surface/contracts.json` L108 is unchanged and no regeneration is owed. The dev's `check:generated` report and the green `Type Check · source gates` run on the head agree.
4. **Member type derived from the wire schema, not hand-spelled — right, and the right side.** `ExplainRequest` is `z.input` of `ExplainRequestSchema` (`explain.zod.ts` L325), the caller-written shape, which is what a caller-side request type must mirror. For this member the choice is also immaterial: `recordIds` carries no `.default()` or `.transform()` (L303), so input and output are both `string[] | undefined`. The test pin spells `z.input` explicitly. Deriving ONLY this member is correct: the contract's `operation` is deliberately `ExplainOperation | string` (L160) against the schema's closed enum, so a whole-interface derivation would be a narrowing.
5. **`import type { EXPLAIN_BATCH_MAX_RECORD_IDS }` (a const imported type-only, used in a `{@link}`) — sound under this repo's config.** TypeScript admits a type-only import of a value declaration; a `{@link}` reference satisfies `noUnusedLocals` (tsconfig.base.json L24); the base config sets neither `verbatimModuleSyntax` nor `isolatedModules`, and the root eslint config carries no `consistent-type-imports` or `no-unused-vars` rule. The pattern already ships on `main`: `packages/spec/src/data/masked-field-types.ts` L70 imports `SECRET_MASK` type-only and references it only in `{@link SECRET_MASK}` (L9, L106). `Lint · ESLint` and `Type Check · source gates` are green on the head. Emitted d.ts: declaration emit keeps an import specifier only when an emitted declaration references it, so the JSDoc-only specifier may be elided from the bundled `contracts/index.d.ts` and the `{@link}` text then resolves nowhere in a consumer's hover — cosmetic, identical to the `SECRET_MASK` precedent, and invisible to the api-surface gate, which records names. Not a defect.
6. **The doc comment's claims hold against the cited code.** Mutual exclusion: wire `superRefine` at `explain.zod.ts` L313–323; reference refusal at `security-plugin-explain-access.ts` L142–145. Cap and min: L303 (`.min(1).max(EXPLAIN_BATCH_MAX_RECORD_IDS)`, constant = 200 at L257). Ordering: `ExplainDecisionSchema.records` L419–430; engine `explain-engine.ts` L2510 `records: recordIds.map(...)` — same length, per position, duplicates per position; REST L280–285 relays and fail-closes a missing position. "An implementation may ignore it; the REST door then asks per id": `security-routes.ts` L279 call, L280 length check, L288–296 per-id loop. The PR body's line citations (L256–299, L279, L280, L289–296; L128, L142–145, L526–527) are accurate on 29000bb1.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/29297-explain-access-request-record-ids.md`: `@objectstack/spec: patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; the PR body carries the same two lines. Right: an optional member on a published contract interface widens the accepted set and refuses nothing; no authorable metadata key, value or default moves (`recordIds` is a wire-schema member the protocol already carried, as triage 6576596125 ruled, not a new protocol key), so `none` takes `patch` under Post-Task Checklist #3 (a non-protocol widening ships `patch`). Only `@objectstack/spec` moves; no runtime package changes. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- The changeset's statements ("a type-level test holds the two equal", "every request that compiled before still compiles", "no runtime change") are each true of the tree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation 1 (member-level derivation, not whole-interface)** — accepted; see ①4. Whole-interface derivation would turn `operation` into the closed enum, a narrowing the card did not order.
- **Dev deviation 2 (`main` moved 16 commits after the branch point; not merged in)** — verified: `git log 32912139..origin/main` on the contract, its test, `explain.zod.ts`, the REST route, the three plugin-security files and `api-surface/contracts.json` lists zero commits (origin/main `8ca9dd7b`, 16 commits since base). Accepted.
- **Dev deviation 3 (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally)** — closed by the head: `Lint & Repo Gates` is `success`, and the diff emits no JavaScript.
- **Dev deviation 4 (plugin-sharing, service-storage, plugin-audit not run locally)** — accepted at the type reading in ①2; `Type Check · workspace` and `Test Core (1–8/8)` were still `in_progress` at read time and are the gate of record for it.
- **Dev deviation 5 (no MCP writes for assignee/reviewer)** — not a contract matter; correct under the order.
- **Open question (A: member-level + pin, vs B: whole-interface)** — A, for the reason the dev gives and ①4 confirms; B is a narrowing in widening's clothing.
- **Card acceptance** — `recordIds?: string[]`: the PR's `ExplainRequest['recordIds']` is pinned equal to `string[] | undefined`, which is the same member with drift protection. Doc comment: exclusive with `recordId`, capped by the wire constant (linked), answered by `records`, implementation may ignore it with the REST per-id fallback named — all four present (L166–181). `Clause-②`/`Metadata-protocol` declared on both the PR body and the changeset; `check:api-surface` agrees (①3). No runtime change: the diff touches no runtime file.
- **Check-runs on 29000bb1 at 2026-11-02T16:02Z** — `success`: Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, the three scoped lint runs, Type Check · source gates, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build UI Deps, Plan Test Core shards, Auto Label, Flag docs, filter. `in_progress`: Build Core, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Test Core (1–8/8), Test UI (1–16/16), Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI. `skipped`: the opt-in and docs-only runs. No run is red. The queue's required set is not yet fully concluded; this record judges the contract, and the queue guard reads the runs.

### ④ Design judgment

The hits file holds against the ruling it implements (card #29297, the follow-up the #29208 landing record owed) and against its first consumers (the REST explain route and the reference `SecurityPlugin` service). Tried to break it on: optionality (pinned by the `{} extends Pick` alias, which `toEqualTypeOf` alone could not hold); input-vs-output side (①4); the `readonly` mismatch between the reference body's parameter and the contract (`string[]` is assignable to `readonly string[]`, so an implementer typed either way compiles; the ablation to `readonly string[]` on the contract side reds the pin, as reported); excess-property behaviour of the plugin's spread wiring (a spread is never excess-checked, so the member reaches the body at runtime — see should-fix 2); ordering and length (①6); the d.ts (①5). None breaks it.

**Must-fix:** none.

**Should-fix:**
1. (hits file, L173) "Mutually exclusive with `recordId`: a request carrying both is refused" is stated as a property of the contract, while L177–180 lets an implementation ignore `recordIds` — an implementation that ignores the member cannot refuse the mixed request. Say who refuses: the wire schema at the REST door and the reference implementation; a direct kernel caller must send one spelling, never both. Prose precision only; the semantics declared are the ones both readers enforce.
2. (outside hits, plugin-security) `SecurityPlugin.explainAccessForCaller`'s own parameter type (`security-plugin.ts` L2377) still omits `recordIds` while the extracted body it delegates to reads it (L128) and the service wiring passes it through a spread. Nothing is wrong at runtime or in this PR; it is the same contract-vs-code gap this card closed, one package down. Follow-up card for `domain:server`, not a rider on this PR.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `57913a379525abcbfb63ab4fba331fda9b2ce136`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts + packages/rest/src/security-routes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-explain-access.ts, packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts (all three byte-identical between 29000bb1 and 57913a37). The changeset and `security-service.test.ts` are unchanged on this head and remain the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Delta record: one commit on 29000bb1 (`docs(spec): say who refuses a request carrying both recordId and recordIds`), +4/-1 in the doc comment of `ExplainAccessRequest.recordIds` (L174–177). The record on 29000bb1 stands for everything it judged; this record judges the delta and re-reads the gates on the new head. Net diff against `main`: the same 3 files, +89/-2.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **No accept-set or public-surface change — right.** The commit edits JSDoc prose only: no member, type, import or export moves. `ExplainAccessRequest (interface)` stays the api-surface row it was; `recordIds?: ExplainRequest['recordIds']` is unchanged, so the type pins in `security-service.test.ts` hold as before. The emitted d.ts changes only in comment text.
2. **The new sentences are each true of the cited code.** "The wire schema refuses a request carrying both at the REST explain route": `ExplainRequestSchema` `superRefine` (`explain.zod.ts` L313–323) is what the route's `safeParse` runs at `security-routes.ts` L236, and a failure answers the 400 at L249–253 before any service call. "The reference security service refuses it too": `security-plugin-explain-access.ts` L142–145 throws on `recordIds` beside `recordId`. "An implementation that ignores `recordIds` does not": true by construction, and it is the exact gap the earlier wording papered over. "A direct caller of `explain` sends one spelling, never both": the caller-side instruction the contract can actually bind.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right: `@objectstack/spec: patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the changeset and the PR body. A doc-comment edit moves no level. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Should-fix 1 of the 29000bb1 record** — resolved. The sentence no longer promises a refusal of every implementation; it names the two readers that refuse (wire schema at the REST door, reference service) and the one that cannot, and tells a direct caller what to send. This is the wording the earlier record asked for.
- **Should-fix 2 of the 29000bb1 record** (`SecurityPlugin.explainAccessForCaller`'s own parameter type omits `recordIds`, `security-plugin.ts` L2377) — unchanged, and correctly so: it was named as a follow-up card for plugin-security, not a rider on this PR.
- **`main` movement** — origin/main `94d3e254` at read time; zero commits on the contract, `explain.zod.ts`, the REST route or the reference implementation since the branch point `32912139`.
- **Check-runs on 57913a37 at 2026-11-02T16:32Z** — every non-skipped run `completed`/`success`, the queue's required set included: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check (and its four sub-runs: workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Test Core (and 1–8/8), Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint UI (skipped by paths filter), Type Check UI, Test UI (and 1–16/16), Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI; plus Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint · ESLint and the scoped lint runs. `skipped`: the opt-in and docs-only runs only. No run is red or in progress.

### ④ Design judgment

The hits file still holds against the card's acceptance and against its two consumers; the delta makes the one doc claim that over-promised precise, and introduces no new claim the cited code does not back. Tried to break it on: whether "at the REST explain route" misattributes the refusal (it does not — the route runs the schema, the schema carries the refine, L236/L313–323); whether the sentence now under-promises for the reference implementation (it does not — L142–145 throws before any evaluation); whether a `{@link}` or import changed (none did). Nothing new is broken.

**Must-fix:** none.

**Should-fix:** none on this PR (should-fix 2 of the prior record remains a plugin-security follow-up card).

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：安全服务契约里的 `ExplainAccessRequest` 类型加了一个可选成员 `recordIds`（一次解释多条记录的权限），类型直接取自线协议 schema，两边不会再走样。
- 为什么改：线协议 `ExplainRequestSchema` 早已接受 `recordIds`，REST 解释接口和参考实现也都在用；契约类型却没声明，第三方实现看不到批量入口，调用方只能绕过类型。
- 风险与回滚：只改 TypeScript 类型和注释，运行时零改动；以前能编译的调用照样能编译。回滚就是 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts` 的 `ExplainAccessRequest.recordIds` 及其注释。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/contracts/security-service.test.ts`，预期全部通过（类型钉子确认成员可选、且与 schema 输入类型相等）。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

席位意见：可落地。契约复审在 29000bb1 判 PASS（6581862373），席位要的一句注释修正已在现 head 由同一复审者 delta 复审 PASS（本 PR 上一条记录）。CI 全绿。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · `domain:spec#4` · head `57913a37`

1. **Shape:** draft, base `main`, `Fixes #29297`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and `Skills-docs: none — …` sit at line start in the body; the changeset `.changeset/29297-explain-access-request-record-ids.md` (`@objectstack/spec` patch) carries the same two lines. 3 files, +89/−2: `security-service.ts`, its test, the changeset, all inside claim 6580454301. No governed path. Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay).
2. **Premise measured:** on `main` `ExplainAccessRequest` declared no `recordIds` while `ExplainRequestSchema` did. The member is now `recordIds?: ExplainRequest['recordIds']` (`ExplainRequest` is the schema's `z.input`); type pins hold it optional and equal to the schema input; the dev's ablation to `readonly string[]` went red. The docblock was checked against the REST route (`safeParse` → 400) and the reference service's refusal.
3. **Gates:** check-runs on `57913a37`: 55 success, 9 skipped (opt-in or path-gated), none failed. Dev ran 79 derived gates on `29000bb1`: 78 exit 0, 1 NOT MEASURED (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, needs a whole-repo build; CI's Build Core is green). `check:api-surface` records interface names only, so nothing regenerates.
4. **Accepted deviations:** only the member is derived, not the whole interface (open question answered A: deriving `operation` would narrow the deliberate `ExplainOperation | string`); no merge of `main` (16 commits, none on the touched files); consumers plugin-sharing, storage and audit left to CI (green); no MCP assignee/reviewer writes (the order forbids them).
5. **Out of scope:** `SecurityPlugin.explainAccessForCaller`'s own parameter type omits `recordIds` → filed #29481 (`domain:server`, Blocked-by #29297). No skills or docs page spells the contract's members (`Skills-docs: none`).
6. **Landing:** not Tier H, under 3000 lines: the seat lands it with `pr_ready` and auto-merge. After merge the seat writes a landing note on #29297 and removes `pm:dispatched`.
